title: Managing a stage boundary: activities, inputs, outputs and RACI
blurb: Place a project manager's end-of-stage action in the right managing a stage boundary activity, including exception plans, and answer RACI questions on evaluating the stage.
question: As a pilot stage ends, the project manager finds a benefit is forecast lower than the business case says, though no tolerance is threatened. Which stage boundary activity handles this, and who is consulted when the end stage report is prepared?

teach.h: What the stage boundary is for
teach.body: Managing a stage boundary gives the board enough information to review the success of the current stage, prepare the next stage plan (which the board then approves in directing a project), review the updated project plan, and confirm that the business case is still justified and the risks acceptable. The project manager runs it at or close to the end of each stage, and also whenever the board asks for an exception plan. It is not used at the end of the final stage: closing a project takes over there.

teach.caption: Fig 18.1 has six activities: the two 'prepare' activities are alternatives at the start. The board then decides in directing a project.

teach.h: Who does what at the boundary
teach.body: Managing a stage boundary is a managing-level process: the project manager prepares the plans, updates the project plan and business case, and evaluates the stage, drawing on team managers, project support and project assurance for input. The board does not act here; it decides in directing a project, when it authorizes a stage or exception plan. Every 'request' activity follows that pattern: the PM asks, the board authorizes.

teach.h: Where the boundaries fall at Wenmoor

items.label: Design and pilot preparation, then SB
Roll-out (final): ends in CP, no SB

teach.caption: Managing a stage boundary is first used at the end of initiation and not at the end of the final stage.

teach.body: As the Eastfield pilot of the single point of access ends, project manager Ellie Chandran plans the final roll-out stage, including the closure work. She updates the project plan with pilot actuals and the new stage forecasts. Staff mileage fell by 8%, not the 15% forecast, so she updates the business case and benefits management approach. She prepares the end stage report, consulting Moira Healy, project support and Neil Ashworth (project assurance), then briefs the board, including a concession on the referral form.

teach.text: Traps: (1) The exception plan is prepared in managing a stage boundary, not in controlling a stage, and only after the board asks for it. (2) A changed benefits forecast is handled in update the business case, not by an exception plan. (3) Closure is planned inside the final stage's plan; there is no separate closure stage and no stage boundary at the end of the final stage. (4) Evaluate the stage: PM responsible; team manager, project support and project assurance consulted.

items: Six activities: prepare next stage plan, prepare exception plan, update the project plan, update the business case, evaluate the stage, request next stage.
Exception plan: requested by the board after an exception report; request recorded in the project log.
Update the business case covers benefits forecast changes and aggregated risk exposure.
Request next stage includes any concessions for off-specifications.
Evaluate the stage RACI: PM responsible; TM, support and assurance consulted.

summary: You can now place any end-of-stage action in the right managing a stage boundary activity, from planning the next stage to briefing the board. You can also answer RACI questions on evaluating the stage from the official row.

A.q: Wenmoor Community Health is introducing a single point of access for referrals. As the Eastfield pilot stage ends, project manager Ellie Chandran produces the plan for the evaluation and roll-out stage, the project's final stage, and includes the handover to the localities and the work to close the project. Which 'managing a stage boundary' activity is she carrying out?
A.why: Prepare next stage plan produces the plan for the next stage near the end of the current one; closure activities are planned in the final stage's plan.

whyNot.0: Update the project plan adds actuals and forecasts to the whole-project plan; Ellie is producing a stage plan.
whyNot.2: An exception plan is prepared only when the board asks for one after an exception report; this stage is ending as planned.
whyNot.3: Evaluate the stage reviews the stage just finishing and produces the end stage report.

A.q: At the end of the Eastfield pilot, Neil Ashworth, Wenmoor's head of internal audit who provides project assurance, offers his views while Ellie Chandran prepares the end stage report. Under the RACI for 'evaluate the stage', what is project assurance's part?
A.why: In evaluate the stage, project assurance is consulted, along with the team manager and project support; the PM is responsible (18.6, table 18.2).

whyNot.0: The project manager is responsible for evaluate the stage.
whyNot.1: Project assurance gives input but does not answer for the activity as a whole.
whyNot.3: Project assurance is consulted, giving input before the report is finished, not just told about it afterwards.

A.q: At the end of the Eastfield pilot, Ellie Chandran adds the pilot's actual dates and costs to the project plan, together with forecasts from the roll-out stage plan. She notes that the revised end date will feed into the business case. Which 'managing a stage boundary' activity is she carrying out?
A.why: Update the project plan includes actual progress from the finishing stage and forecasts from the next stage plan or exception plan; revised costs and dates are then used to update the business case.

whyNot.0: Update the business case uses the revised figures afterwards; adding actuals and forecasts to the plan comes first.
whyNot.1: Evaluate the stage produces the end stage report from the updated plan and business case.
whyNot.2: The roll-out stage plan already exists; Ellie is now updating the project plan with its forecasts.

B.q: During the Eastfield pilot, staff mileage fell by 8% rather than the 15% the business case forecast, though no tolerance is forecast to be exceeded. As the stage ends, Ellie Chandran revises the benefits forecast and updates the benefits management approach with the results of benefits actions so far. Which 'managing a stage boundary' activity is she carrying out?
B.why: Update the business case reflects changes in the project and its environment and updates the benefits management approach with the results of benefits actions. A changed benefits forecast is handled here.

whyNot.1: An exception plan responds to a board request after an exception report; a revised benefits forecast within tolerance does not need one.
whyNot.2: Evaluate the stage reports on the stage using the updated business case; it does not revise the benefits forecast itself.
whyNot.3: Request next stage briefs the board; the business case should already be updated by then.

B.q: Wenmoor's audit committee asks Ellie Chandran who does what when the end stage report for the pilot is prepared. Which statement about the RACI for 'evaluate the stage' is correct?
B.why: In evaluate the stage the PM is responsible, and the team manager, project support and project assurance are consulted (18.6, table 18.2).

whyNot.0: This reverses the roles: the PM is responsible and the team manager consulted.
whyNot.1: The PM is responsible, but project assurance is consulted, not merely informed.
whyNot.3: Project support is consulted; the PM is responsible.

B.q: During the Eastfield pilot, late configuration of the referral module means the stage is forecast to exceed its time tolerance. Ellie Chandran sent an exception report, and the project board has asked her for an exception plan. Which recommended action belongs to the 'prepare exception plan' activity?
options: Raise an exception report setting out the options
Produce a full end stage report in every case
Ask the business layer to approve the revised plan
Record the board's request in the project log
B.why: In prepare exception plan, the board's request is recorded in the project log and the PID is reviewed and updated as needed.

whyNot.0: The exception report was raised earlier, in controlling a stage; this activity responds to the board's request.
whyNot.1: With an exception plan, an end stage report is prepared only if the board requires it.
whyNot.2: This is a stage-level exception, so the project board approves the exception plan in directing a project.

C.q: As the Eastfield pilot ends, Ellie Chandran plans the evaluation and roll-out stage and proposes adding a separate fifth 'closure stage' after roll-out, with its own stage boundary, to hand over the single point of access and close the project. Is this an appropriate application of the 'prepare next stage plan' activity, and why?
options: Yes, because the board must authorize closure as a separate decision
Yes, because a stage boundary is needed at the end of every stage
No, because closure activities belong in the final stage's plan
No, because closure activities are planned in the project plan instead
C.why: Closure activities should be planned as part of the stage plan for the final stage. Closing a project is the last part of the final stage, not a stage of its own.

whyNot.0: The board does authorize closure in directing a project, but that does not make closure a separate stage.
whyNot.1: Managing a stage boundary is not used at the end of the final stage.
whyNot.3: Closure work is planned in detail in the final stage plan, which is produced in this activity.

C.q: Ellie Chandran prepares the end stage report for the Eastfield pilot herself, using the updated business case, project plan and project log. She consults Moira Healy, team manager for the triage hub, project support, and Neil Ashworth, who provides project assurance. Is this an appropriate application of the 'evaluate the stage' activity, and why?
options: Yes, because the PM is responsible and these roles are consulted
Yes, because the end stage report is a time-driven control
No, because assurance should write the report to keep it independent
No, because the report should follow the board's stage authorization
C.why: In evaluate the stage the PM is responsible, consulting the team manager, project support and project assurance, and bases the end stage report on the updated business case, project plan, project log and approaches (table 18.2).

whyNot.1: The verdict is right but the reason is wrong: the end stage report is an event-driven control.
whyNot.2: Project assurance is consulted; the PM is responsible for the end stage report.
whyNot.3: The end stage report is prepared before the request for the next stage, so the board can use it to decide.

C.q: During the Eastfield pilot, the medical director accepted that the e-referral form could go live without a field for carers to refer directly, to be added later. Ellie Chandran asks the board to authorize the roll-out stage and briefs them on performance, the next stage and the resources needed, but does not mention the missing field. Is this an appropriate application of the 'request next stage' activity, and why?
options: Yes, because the board authorizes the next stage in directing a project
Yes, because the concession is already recorded in the issue register
No, because the end stage report should go to the business layer
No, because she should confirm concessions for off-specifications
C.why: When requesting the next stage, the PM briefs the board on stage performance, the next stage, people and resources and readiness, and confirms any concessions for off-specifications during the stage.

whyNot.0: The board does authorize the next stage, but that does not excuse leaving out the concession from the briefing.
whyNot.1: The concession may be recorded, but the request still needs to highlight it to the board.
whyNot.2: The end stage report goes to the project board, which decides on the next stage.

reteach.title: Close one stage, open the next
reteach.question: Picture the PM at the end of a stage preparing a pack for the board. What goes in the pack, and in what order is it built?

blocks.body: First the PM plans what comes next: the next stage plan, or an exception plan if the board asked for one. Then the project plan is updated with actuals and forecasts, and the business case with new costs, benefits forecasts and risk exposure. Then the stage is evaluated in the end stage report. Finally the PM asks the board to authorize the next stage, highlighting any concessions.

items.label: next stage plan or exception plan

blocks.text: Evaluate the stage: PM responsible; team manager, project support and project assurance consulted. Benefits forecast changes go into update the business case.

explain.body: Prepare next stage plan produces the next stage's plan near the end of the current stage; closure activities go into the final stage's plan. Prepare exception plan is used when the board, after an exception report, asks for one; its approval marks a stage boundary for the revised stage.

explain.h: Next stage plan or exception plan?

test.q: Wenmoor's trust board asks when the detailed plan for the evaluation and roll-out stage will be produced. Which answer is correct?
options: Near the end of the pilot, in managing a stage boundary
During initiation, alongside the project plan
At the start of roll-out, in controlling a stage
When the board asks for it after an exception report
test.why: Each delivery stage plan after initiation is produced near the end of the previous stage, in prepare next stage plan.

whyNot.1: Initiation produces the project plan; stage plans for later stages are produced at each stage boundary.
whyNot.2: Controlling a stage runs the stage once its plan is authorized; the plan is produced before that.
whyNot.3: A plan asked for after an exception report is an exception plan, not the normal next stage plan.

explain.h: Updating the project plan and business case
explain.body: Update the project plan adds actual progress and forecasts from the next stage or exception plan. Update the business case uses the revised costs and dates, reflects changes inside and outside the project, updates the benefits management approach, and assesses the aggregated risk exposure from the project log.

test.q: At the end of the Eastfield pilot, Ellie Chandran reviews the risk register and other records in the project log to judge the total risk exposure the project now carries, so the board can see whether it is still acceptable. Which activity is she carrying out?
test.why: Update the business case includes assessing the aggregated risk exposure from the project log, so the board can confirm the project is still justified and the risks acceptable.

whyNot.0: Update the project plan adds actuals and forecasts of time and cost, not the overall risk exposure.
whyNot.2: Evaluate the stage uses the updated business case to write the end stage report.
whyNot.3: Prepare next stage plan plans the next stage's products and work.

explain.body: Evaluate the stage produces the end stage report from the updated business case, project plan, project log and approaches. Request next stage briefs the board on the stage's performance, the next stage, the people and resources needed, readiness to proceed, and any concessions for off-specifications.

test.q: Ellie Chandran is preparing to brief the Wenmoor project board in the 'request next stage' activity. Which item belongs in that briefing?
options: Follow-on actions for every open issue and risk
The latest checkpoint report from each team
Results of the post-project benefits reviews
test.why: Request next stage includes confirming any concessions for off-specifications during the stage, alongside performance, the next stage, resources and readiness.

whyNot.0: Follow-on action recommendations for all open issues and risks are a closing a project objective; the request next stage briefing covers performance, the next stage, resources, readiness and concessions.
whyNot.2: Checkpoint reports go to the PM; the board gets summaries, not each team's checkpoint.
whyNot.3: Post-project benefits reviews happen after the project closes, so there are no results yet.

explain.body: For evaluate the stage, the PM is responsible; the team manager, project support and project assurance are consulted. The board then uses the end stage report in directing a project. For any other stage boundary row, use table 18.2 in the open book.

test.q: Wenmoor's project support officer drafts most of the end stage report for the pilot, and Ellie Chandran reviews, completes and issues it. Under the RACI for 'evaluate the stage', which role is responsible?
test.why: The PM is responsible for evaluate the stage even when project support helps draft the report; support is consulted (18.6, table 18.2).

whyNot.0: Project support is consulted in evaluate the stage; drafting help does not change the RACI.
whyNot.2: The team manager is consulted in evaluate the stage.
whyNot.3: Project assurance is consulted in evaluate the stage.
